canonical_fact: The PVM is a deterministic 64-bit RISC-V-derived machine model used for JAM service and authorizer execution.
misconceptions: PVM execution may depend on host wall-clock time or filesystem state.
title: PVM machine

canonical_fact: JAM's PVM is based on the RV64EM RISC-V profile defined by the Gray Paper rather than an unrestricted host CPU environment.
title: RV64EM profile

canonical_fact: Executable service logic is represented as a protocol-defined PVM program blob that is decoded into code, memory layout and jump-related metadata.
title: PVM program blob

canonical_fact: PVM execution state includes a fixed register file of 64-bit values used by instructions and invocation conventions.
title: PVM registers

canonical_fact: PVM execution includes paged RAM with explicit readable and writable validity rules enforced by the machine semantics.
title: PVM memory

canonical_fact: The PVM program counter identifies the current instruction position and is updated deterministically by each machine step.
title: Program counter

canonical_fact: PVM execution tracks remaining gas and halts or errors when execution cannot pay the gas required by the next operation.
title: PVM gas counter

canonical_fact: The Gray Paper defines a whole-program PVM state-transition function by iterating single-step machine transitions until a terminal condition.
title: Whole-program transition

canonical_fact: The Refine invocation convention initializes a PVM execution environment and exposes the host functions appropriate to in-core service refinement.

relations.statement: The Refine entry point is executed using the Refine-specific PVM invocation convention.

title: Refine PVM invocation

canonical_fact: The Accumulate invocation convention executes the service's stateful entry point with accumulation-specific arguments and host functions.

relations.statement: The Accumulate entry point is executed using the Accumulate-specific PVM invocation convention.

title: Accumulate PVM invocation

canonical_fact: Authorizer logic is executed through a dedicated PVM invocation convention that decides package authorization under bounded resources.
title: Is-Authorized invocation

canonical_fact: PVM host calls are protocol-defined external functions that give service code controlled access to JAM context and state rather than arbitrary operating-system facilities.
misconceptions: PVM code can freely call POSIX or host operating-system APIs.
title: Host call

canonical_fact: The gas-remaining host call lets PVM code query its current deterministic gas budget.
title: Gas-remaining host call

canonical_fact: The lookup-preimage host call retrieves a preimage available in the invocation's permitted lookup context.

relations.statement: Lookup-preimage accesses data from the service preimage system permitted by the invocation context.

title: Lookup-preimage host call

canonical_fact: The historical-lookup-preimage host call queries preimage availability at a permitted historical context rather than assuming latest-state access.
title: Historical-lookup-preimage host call

canonical_fact: The read-storage host call reads service storage during accumulation under the protocol's state-access rules.
misconceptions: Read-storage is available as unrestricted latest-state access during Refine.
title: Read-storage host call

canonical_fact: The write-storage host call mutates service storage during stateful accumulation when the caller has the required authority.

relations.statement: Write-storage mutates service storage in the stateful accumulation environment.

title: Write-storage host call

canonical_fact: The solicit-preimage host call requests that a particular hash and length preimage become available through the service preimage system.
title: Solicit-preimage host call

canonical_fact: The forget-preimage host call changes preimage availability according to the historical retention rules rather than instantly erasing arbitrary history.
title: Forget-preimage host call

canonical_fact: The provide-preimage host call supplies preimage data through the protocol-defined accumulation interface.
title: Provide-preimage host call

canonical_fact: The transfer host call creates a deferred service-to-service transfer that is processed through accumulation semantics.
misconceptions: The transfer host call directly completes the receiving service’s state transition inside the same instruction.
title: Transfer host call

canonical_fact: The new-service host call creates a service account subject to JAM's service-index, balance and privilege rules.
title: New-service host call

canonical_fact: The upgrade-service host call changes the service code identity and related execution parameters under the permitted authority model.
title: Upgrade-service host call

canonical_fact: The assign-core host call allows the appropriately privileged service logic to alter core-related authorization assignment state.
title: Assign-core host call

canonical_fact: The export-segment host call emits a fixed-size segment from Refine so it can enter JAM's distributed data-availability path and be imported by later work.

relations.statement: Export-segment emits data that becomes a work-package export for later import.

title: Export-segment host call
